change: Attempted an offscreen GL context under WSL2 Ubuntu-24.04 to host the planned EGL render path. Two restarts, wsl --update --pre-release, every platform and driver override.
conclusion: REFUTED. Mesa falls back to a CPU rasterizer under every override; the root cause is below Mesa, so no Mesa-level fix exists. CUDA is unaffected - different ioctl path. All rendering moved to native Windows and EGL is out of the project. Settled; do not re-litigate.

change: Timed mjr_readPixels per call in isolation at 64x64, then toggled MuJoCo's visual defaults to find the fixed cost. offsamples 4 -> 0, shadowsize 4096 -> 0.
conclusion: MuJoCo discussion #2222's ~30 ms per call does not reproduce - off by three orders of magnitude. The real fixed cost was an MSAA resolve forced by offsamples=4. Two-pass render confirmed with 13x margin, so the WGL pbuffer and the single-pass collapse are both cancelled. Promotes <quality offsamples=0 shadowsize=0/> from cosmetic to a hard arm_blocks.xml requirement.

change: Timed mj_step alone on arm_blocks.xml, idle and driven arms, 5x1000 steps resetting every 200, 6 separate processes. Contact guard narrowed to an arm-block geom-pair filter excluding the table.
conclusion: P-6 is not at risk from physics. Contact counts and both fractions came back bit-identical across 6 processes - unseeded determinism. The earlier ncon>0 guard scored both arms at 100% and was vacuous. E-4's 5% is NOT demonstrated for this number: the series had not plateaued after 6 runs and needs a quiescent-machine protocol.

change: Re-measured memory bandwidth and fp16 matmul with the GPU clocked up, in two phases because no single load clocks both domains. Follows a chassis cooling fix.
conclusion: 448 GB/s REFUTED - that figure is the desktop 5060 at 28 Gbps; this Laptop part runs 24, so the ceiling is 384. Every fork-table compute floor rose 45% and CUDA graphs became required on BOTH paths, not just the 144-token one. Cooling alone gave 9x on matmul while every instantaneous throttle flag read Not Active - the evidence was in the PERFORMANCE counters. Also refutes pstate==P0 as a validity gate: pstate follows the memory domain and reads P4 during correct compute-bound work.

change: Timed the full per-frame generation cost on the real scene - mj_step, mjv_updateScene, two-pass render with the segmentation pass, and readback - 5x1000 calls through the XML 'main' camera.
conclusion: Parallel generation is NOT needed - the trigger does not fire. 300k frames in about a minute single-threaded. mjv_updateScene was the last day-1 unknown and is negligible. p99 exceeds the whole frame budget but P-6 is throughput, not latency, so at 1% weight it costs ~10% of the mean. Taken while the GPU was thermally capped, so this is a pessimistic bound.

change: Added a <visual> block with offsamples=0, shadowsize=0 and an ambient-only headlight (diffuse and specular both zero).
conclusion: The ambient-only headlight is what collapses the palette: diffuse light shades per face, so one rgba becomes three entries per box. castshadow=false was listed as the fix and is wrong - it is a <light> attribute and MuJoCo's compiler rejects it on a geom. The contact figure is a full-torque drive, not the 50/50 policy, so it is indicative only.

change: Ported the offscreen context to C++20 with four fatal startup checks: renderer deny-list, currentBuffer, viewport against the scene's offwidth/offheight, and mjr_getError. Built /W4 /WX clean in both configurations.
conclusion: F-3 holds from C++, not just from the Python probe. All four checks are fatal at startup, so a software renderer or a silent 640x480 fallback cannot reach the data run. Deny-list on the two software spellings, not an allow-list on 'RTX 5060', which would fail on any other perfectly good machine.

change: Added the base-3 action encoding and its round-trip self-check. Built /W4 /WX clean in both configurations.
conclusion: All 9 actions decode to distinct ctrl pairs and re-encode to the same index. Gotcha recorded: jnt_qposadr and jnt_dofadr DIVERGE for free joints - block1 is 9 vs 8, block2 16 vs 14, because a free joint is 7 wide in qpos and 6 in qvel. Never compute either address; always read the array.

change: Checked which sanitizers MSVC actually provides, then built and ran under each.
conclusion: E-3 DROPS its UBSan half rather than adding a clang-cl configuration. /fsanitize=undefined and /fsanitize=leak are listed only as possible future work. The one relevant UB class - signed overflow on shard offsets across 3.6 GB - is closed by typing every offset int64_t plus a write-site bounds assert, which runs in the optimised build where a side-configuration sanitizer would not. ASan also needs /Zi (C5072 is fatal under /WX) and its runtime DLL copied beside the binary.

change: A/B on steps_per_episode with steering-off (reach_noise_prob=1.0) as the control that separates 'reach is broken' from 'episode too short'.
conclusion: steps_per_episode=200 REFUTED. 200 steps is 0.4 s of sim time and the arm cannot cross to a block from a random start angle. Changed to 600 x 500 episodes - the same 300k frames - which also cuts ctx=15 boundary loss from 7.5% to 2.5%. The steering-off control gives a 6x separation in median closest approach, so the reach itself works.

change: Swept the Jacobian deadband and per-digit versus whole-action noise across 14 configurations at 200 episodes x 600 steps.
conclusion: F-5's 2.5 ceiling is set at the measured knee, not at a rounder number: arrival is flat at 42.5-44% down to ratio 2.44, then falls off. Per-digit noise dominates whole-action noise at every setting once the deadband is on, and every no-deadband configuration is strictly dominated. Below ~1.7 is unreachable by any tuning - a two-link planar arm reaching outward turns both hinges the same way, which is kinematics. Shipped jacobian_deadband=0.04, reach_digit_noise_prob=0.15.

run: policy_dry_run at F-5's own sample size
change: Ran at the 2,000-episode sample size F-5 actually names, twice, to check both the thresholds and replay.
conclusion: F-5 passes with margin on both thresholds, and the two passes are identical over 1.2M actions. Compliance costs arrival 44% -> 35.7% and median closest 0.042 -> 0.052 m; arrival is a diagnostic, not a requirement. The 200-episode startup smoke run reads ratio 2.30 / min share 6.55% and is marked INDICATIVE - at 200 episodes the ratio moves ~0.2 between samples, which is why F-5 names 2,000.

change: Added the segmentation pass and the id-colour decode. Dry run drives actuator 0 at full torque for 1500 steps, with three fatal checks around a teleported block.
conclusion: The id-colour decode r + 256g + 65536b is verified from C++ as well as Python, and identically under both build types, ASan-clean. Both rates are INDICATIVE, not the verdict: the sweep is not the 50/50 policy, and a block punted off the table reads 0 for every remaining frame. New gotcha: the segmentation pass leaves the offscreen framebuffer holding id colours, so the RGB readback MUST precede Truth::read - reversed, the shard stores id colours and nothing downstream fails.

change: Moved block0 to negative y after it read 0 visible px in the resting pose, which made F-7 score off one static configuration rather than off the arm moving.
conclusion: F-7 now measures the arm passing in front of a block rather than one static pose. Cause: the camera sits at y=-0.5 looking toward +y and the arm rests along +x at y=0, so any block at small positive y is behind it. F-6 is still 10x its floor and F-5's verdict is unchanged. Do not flip the sign back. F-7 keeps one known bias - a block knocked off the table reads zero forever and counts as occluded.

change: Ran the full generation loop on a small 6-episode config, optimised and under ASan, then read both blobs back in numpy. The config hash for this run was not recorded at the time.
conclusion: ASan-clean. F-4 holds at the PIXEL level - two runs at one seed produced byte-identical .pixels and .meta, which is stronger than policy_dry_run's action-sequence check. The sidecar is absent until commit(), checked at the one moment it is observable. Two decisions came out of it: data_hash is passed in as a required flag and never recomputed in C++, and shards rotate only on episode boundaries because Policy is seeded per shard. The one-shard F-6/F-7 figures here are SUPERSEDED by the full-set gate run below.

change: Full 300,000-frame generation at base.json, git ce5c193, then a second complete run at the same seed for the replay check.
conclusion: GATE MET, all three conditions: 300k frames on disk, deterministic replay, hardware render confirmed by GL_RENDERER. Replay gave bit-identical .pixels and .meta for all 7 shards - determinism demonstrated over the real dataset, not a sample. data_hash and git_sha identical across all 7 sidecars. CORRECTS a small-sample figure: F-6 and F-7 read 62.4% and 40.3% off a single 1,200-frame shard, 3x the full-set values. Quote the full-set numbers, not those.

change: Added the memmap reader and episode-aware window sampler, then measured loader throughput against P-7's 30-minute epoch budget. Single-threaded, no DataLoader workers.
conclusion: F-8 holds: 448 sampled records decode identically through the structured dtype and through an independent struct.unpack at the documented offsets. Needs NO workers, prefetch or caching layer - 3.43 GiB of pixels in 31.6 GB of RAM means the page cache holds the whole set. Gotcha found by getting it wrong: slicing an np.memmap returns a lazy view and touches no pages, so a first probe reported 3.4M fps having timed slice arithmetic. Row order settled - the blob is bottom-up and the flip belongs in the sampler, not in Shard.pixels. Split is by episode, hashed; by frame it would leak.

change: Added the measurement vector and both modes, then ran F-9's threshold sweep. F-2 over all 300,000 frames; the sweep over 8,000 frames drawn from 500 windows.
conclusion: F-2 holds over the WHOLE set, not a sample. Mode 2 is validated directly against ground truth: pixel-only px_count equals the segmentation visible_px exactly on 100% of 6,000 block readings. offpalette_px at tau 8 is the viable verdict expression with 11x headroom. px_count is RULED OUT as a per-frame threshold - the smallest count on a block ground truth calls visible is 1 px with margin 0, because F-7 makes partial occlusion common. Two corrections found by measurement: rgba*255 does not land exactly and not by a modellable rule, so nearest-palette-by-argmin is load-bearing; and the palette needs a 7th entry the XML cannot name - the black void past the table edge is 14.1% of every frame. Thresholds are PRINTED, NOT written into config: the build order recalibrates against Phase 1 tokenizer reconstructions first.

change: Settled sim.action_hold_steps, a guess since it was written. Settling time by driving one joint from rest and reading the step count at 63% of terminal velocity at four link1 angles; agreement swept over nine holds at 60 episodes x 600 steps; then a gear/damping scaling sweep to test whether the agreement-vs-coverage trade is forced.
conclusion: The ~15-step estimate was wrong: it read dof_armature=0.01 as the inertia, but armature is the term ADDED to the mass-matrix diagonal, not the diagonal. Joint0 takes 21-34 steps depending on link1's angle; joint1 takes 12 and is configuration-independent. The first-order M/b prediction matches every measurement, so both are trustworthy. Two consequences. Q-4's 90% bar is above its own ceiling - ground-truth frames score 83.1% at the shipped hold, so a model reproducing the simulator exactly fails Q-4 by 7 points; that is a requirement defect, not a dataset defect. And no hold satisfies both Q-4 and window coverage at the shipped physics: agreement reaches 90% only at hold 60, where window coverage has fallen from 62.1% to 19.4%. The trade is NOT forced, though - tau = M/damping while v_term = gear*ctrl/damping, so scaling gear and damping together shortens the transient at constant arm speed, and gear 2->6 with damping 0.5->1.5 gives 90.3% agreement at hold 15 with 83.3% coverage. NOT APPLIED: it is a scene edit, so it moves data_hash, invalidates the 300k set and needs F-5, F-6 and F-7 re-verified. action_hold_steps left at 20 pending that decision - now a known trade rather than a guess.

run: PHASE 0 GATE re-run at gear 6 / damping 1.5, action_hold_steps 15
change: Paths B and C from D1/D2 together. Scene scales gear and damping 3x each (2/0.5 -> 6/1.5), which holds terminal velocity at 4.0 rad/s while cutting joint0's settling time from 34 steps to 12; action_hold_steps 20 -> 15; and Q-4 restated from an absolute 90% to 90% of the simulator's own agreement on the same subset. Regenerated all 300k frames at the new data_hash, generated a second time at the same seed for the replay check, then re-ran every M-tier check over the full set.
conclusion: All three gate conditions hold again and every M-tier row re-verified. The two numbers the change was for both moved: Q-4's ground-truth ceiling, measured on the shipped 50/50 mix over 421,701 driven (frame, joint) pairs, is 91.5% against 83.1% before - it now clears the old absolute 90% outright, so the relative restatement is no longer load-bearing for passing, only for honesty; and ctx=15 window coverage is 60.9% against 41.3%, a 1.47x increase in windows carrying any evidence of what an action does. Costs are small and both expected: F-6 fell 20.69% -> 16.63%, still 3.3x its floor, and throughput fell from 6,775 fps because a more responsive arm makes more contacts for the solver to resolve. Scripted-reach arrival ROSE, 36.4% -> 40.0%, which is the same responsiveness helping the reach close. data_hash moved 0259947e -> 219ab0af and validator_hash with it, so every artifact keyed to the old set is unreachable by construction - the hash tree working, not a mess to clean up.

run: E-2 clean build from scratch, sim/build and sim/build-asan
change: Cloned the branch into an empty directory that had never held this project, then ran the documented CMake commands for both build types, ran both binaries, and generated a 40-frame shard with each. E-2 had never been executed - the README's Build section said 'Not yet implemented'.
conclusion: E-2 MET. Both build types configure, compile /W4 /WX clean and run from an empty directory with no manual step beyond the four commands now in README. Three things only a from-empty run shows. (1) The build CANNOT live under %TEMP%: MSBuild's FileTracker fails FTK1011 inside CMake's compiler probe, so it reports as 'no working C++ compiler' rather than as a path problem - this cost the first attempt. (2) sim/build and sim/build-asan keep separate _deps trees, so the second configure re-downloads MuJoCo and re-clones GLFW; nothing is shared and nothing is vendored. (3) The ASan run over the same 40 frames is sanitizer-clean and its .pixels and .meta are BYTE-IDENTICAL to the Release build's, which widens F-4 from 'same build twice' to 'two build configurations' on one toolchain. AND IT FOUND A LIVE PROVENANCE BUG: asked for its data_hash, the clean clone answered 18a76531 where the worktree answered 219ab0af - see the next entry.

run: data_hash CRLF/LF fork, found by the E-2 clean clone
change: Asked the fresh E-2 clone and this worktree, standing on the same commit, for load('mirage/configs/base.json').data_hash. They disagreed. Diagnosed the cause, then normalised CRLF out of the scene XML inside mirage.config.scene_bytes, renormalised 12 worktree files to LF, and regenerated the whole dataset.
conclusion: REFUTES the assumption that .gitattributes closes this. data_hash hashes the scene XML's RAW BYTES, so a CRLF working tree and an LF one name different datasets for one byte-identical scene - the exact fork .gitattributes' own comment says must never happen, live in the repo, with the entire 300,000-frame set stamped 219ab0af, a hash no fresh clone could reproduce. Cause: '* text=auto eol=lf' landed in f0cdf09 and git applies eol only at CHECKOUT - it never rewrites a working tree that already exists, so every file already on disk kept the CRLF core.autocrlf=true had given it. git status hid it, because text=auto normalises before comparing, so the tree read clean. Fixed by normalising inside config.load rather than by trusting the attribute: provenance now depends on nothing a checkout has to honour, and config's self-check asserts a CRLF scene hashes as its LF twin. GENERAL LESSON: a hash over raw file bytes is only reproducible if something normalises those bytes, and 'git handles it' is a convention, not a guarantee. Nothing but a checkout that had never been touched could have surfaced this - every existing tree agreed with itself.

run: PHASE 0 GATE re-run at data_hash 18a76531, with D3's scripted flag
change: Regenerated all 300k frames after the CRLF fix, with D3's is_scripted flag now packed into contact_mask bit 7. Generated a second time at the same seed and SHA256-compared all 14 blobs, then ran both Python self-checks and the ASan build over the writer path.
conclusion: All three gate conditions hold and every M-tier row re-verified. Every measured value is UNCHANGED from the 219ab0af run, which is the expected result: sim/policy.cpp and scene/arm_blocks.xml are untouched (git diff is empty over both), so only the contact_mask byte's high bit differs. F-5 is therefore unchanged by inspection rather than by re-measurement - it is the same computation that read min share 7.17% / ratio 2.15. D3's flag reads correctly: the scripted bit is CONSTANT across every frame of all 500 episodes - asserted per episode, not in aggregate, because a per-frame bug would still leave a plausible mix at the dataset level - and 53.2% of episodes are scripted. That F-6 still reads 16.63% rather than jumping past 50% is the evidence that every reader masks the flag off. The record stays 46 bytes. ASan-clean, both C++ self-checks passing, including the writer check that now alternates the flag and would fail a writer that hardcoded either value.

run: mirage/fixtures - committed self-check fixture, and validator.offpalette_tau
change: Two structural fixes. tau moved out of three validator.py default arguments into validator.offpalette_tau in base.json, read through Config. And a 40-frame fixture - 2 episodes x 20 steps, written by the freshly built mirage_sim.exe from the E-2 run above - committed under mirage/fixtures/, with both self-checks falling back to it when data/shards holds no committed shard.
conclusion: Both self-checks now run in a clone that has never generated anything, which is what F-8's and F-9's acceptance tests being 'python -m mirage.data' and 'python -m mirage.validator' requires - previously both died on FileNotFoundError in every fresh clone, every worktree and any CI. The fixture is real writer output, not synthesised from meta_dtype plus random pixels: F-8 is a claim about the bytes shard_writer.cpp emits, and a synthesised shard would agree with the reader by construction. It costs 4.9 KB packed. Three checks are skipped on the fixture and say so - F-6, F-7, and the episode-level train/val split - because they are claims about the dataset and 40 frames from 2 episodes can only pass or fail them by luck; the split's hash function is instead checked directly over 4,000 synthetic ids, which needs no data at all. VALIDATOR_HASH MOVED, which is the entire point of the tau change: with tau in code, editing it left validator_hash unchanged and two Q-3 coherence-horizon rows taken at different taus would have claimed to be comparable. The VALUE stays uncalibrated until the Phase 1 recalibration - this moved where the number lives, not what it is.

change: Decomposed F-7's occlusion rate over all 300,000 frames into occlusion the block recovers from and a block that never returns, using a reversed cumulative maximum over visible_px per episode. Then projected every block into the camera frustum to say whether the terminal cases had left the table or left the view. No regeneration - the split is recoverable from the shards on disk.
conclusion: REFUTES the recorded cause. The knocked-off-table bias in the checklist's Tier 5 does not exist: NO block has ever left the table, 0 of 900,000 block-frames, worst reach 0.446 m against a 1.2 m half-extent with an arm that reaches 0.33 m. The is_on_table field this project had been reserving for the next regeneration would have separated nothing, and a regeneration is what it would have cost to find that out. The bias itself is real and bigger than the framing implied: 14.48 of F-7's 19.83 points are a block that never returns, so 73% of the headline number is not occlusion. The honest rate is 5.35%, still over the 3% floor but at 1.8x rather than 6.6x - quote that one. The cause is the CAMERA: 12.66% of frames have a block outside the 45-degree frustum, and only 3.56% are terminal with the block still in frame, which is a block parked behind the arm or another block. The projection is validated against the renderer rather than trusted - it agrees on 99.9988% of frames where a block rendered a pixel - and it needs the cube's circumradius as a margin, because blocks reach within 0.196 m of a camera at y=-0.5 and at that range a centre leaves the frustum while a corner is still rendering. A first attempt without that margin disagreed with the renderer on 30% of frames and its own self-check caught it. NO NEW FIELD AND NO REGENERATION: the split falls out of visible_px alone, so Q-6 can score object permanence on occlusion events that actually end, over the shards that already exist. LEFT OPEN: whether F-7's acceptance test should be restated to exclude terminal runs, the way Q-4 was restated once its bar was measured against its own ceiling. That is an M-tier requirement decision, F-7 passes either way, and the numbers are recorded so it can be made on them.

change: Restated an M-tier requirement on the previous entry's measurement. F-7 now counts only occlusion the block recovers from. Requirement reworded, the validator's acceptance check rewritten to score per episode, the config key renamed occlusion_rate_min -> recoverable_occlusion_rate_min, and the split moved into mirage.data.seen_later so the validator and bench/occlusion_probe.py share one implementation.
conclusion: The bar did not move - the quantity it applies to did. A block reading zero pixels for the rest of an episode is gone, not occluded, and Q-6 cannot score object permanence on an event that never ends; 73% of the old count was exactly that. F-7 passes at 5.35% against the unchanged 3% floor. THE MARGIN IS THE THING TO CARRY FORWARD: 1.8x, not the 6.6x the old number implied, so a scene edit that reduces genuine occlusion has far less room than anyone reading 19.83% would have assumed. THE CONFIG KEY RENAME IS LOAD-BEARING, not cosmetic: the threshold value is unchanged, so without the rename validator_hash would have stayed put while the measurement under it changed meaning, and two incomparable F-7 rows would have claimed to be comparable - the exact failure D9 moved tau into config to prevent. data_hash is untouched, so no regeneration. CROSS-CHECKED: the validator scores per episode over the concatenated shards and the probe scores over a reshaped episode axis, written separately, and they agree at 5.35% to the digit. Precedent for restating a requirement on measurement rather than relaxing it: Q-4, the same week.

change: Re-measured Phase 1's six pre-work numbers against the current dataset, which is what they were flagged for. The regeneration was not the problem. The original k-means run never recorded its initialisation, and that unrecorded choice is worth 2.4-2.9 dB: random seeding reproduces the old figures to within 0.2 dB, k-means++ seeding beats them by 2.6 dB at 512 centroids. Every init-free statistic - the exact-patch dictionary, the patch entropy, the flat-receptive-field share, the edge-error split - reproduces to within 0.03 dB or 0.4 pp, so the regeneration moved patch statistics almost not at all. The k-means-512 floor is 29.02 dB, not 26.39, so gate row 2's bar is +0.98 dB and not +3.6. All 512 centroids stay live under k-means++, so the stated Q-2 collapse risk was an initialisation artifact too.

Phase 1 build order item 1. The offscreen render size is written into model->vis.global.offwidth/offheight from config between mj_loadXML and the GlContext constructor, so scene/arm_blocks.xml stays byte-identical and a second resolution becomes a config-only change instead of one that rehashes the 64x64 dataset. Proved a no-op at 64x64 by regenerating all 300,000 frames and comparing every blob. Also refuted a claim in the structural plan: the plan said neither existing size check loses its teeth, but main.cpp's viewport cross-check and gl_context.cpp's now compare the same two numbers, so it is one fact checked twice.

Phase 1 build order item 2. base.json copied with three values changed - sim.height and sim.width to 96, data.shard_dir to data/shards96 - and the set generated. The generation is the first real exercise of item 1's config-driven offwidth/offheight: the context reports a 96x96 viewport off an XML that still says 64. Both self-checks now take an optional config path so a second resolution can be verified without a throwaway script; an explicit path deliberately skips the fixture fallback. Two recorded figures did not reproduce: generation cost and F-7.
